classification.difficultyReason: Read angles measured from different axis directions, associate cosine and sine with the two coordinates, and apply the quadrant signs while retaining exact trigonometric forms.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ on the unit circle. Find the coordinates of $P$, $Q$ and $R$. Leave your answer in exact form.

spec.description: Unit circle with positive axis arrows, radii to P, Q, R, source angle sectors and exterior point labels. Origin O is omitted under the house graph rule. Ordinary geometry is black and unshaded.
spec.mathematics: Q has standard angle 80 degrees; P is 55 degrees clockwise from positive x; R is 20 degrees below negative x, at standard angle 200 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are shown. No coordinate answers.

answer.worked:
A unit-circle point has coordinates $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Use the reference angle and signs in each quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}P&=(\cos(-55^\circ),\sin(-55^\circ))\\P&=(\cos55^\circ,-\sin55^\circ)\\Q&=(\cos80^\circ,\sin80^\circ)\\R&=(\cos200^\circ,\sin200^\circ)\\R&=(-\cos20^\circ,-\sin20^\circ)\end{align*}$$
